purpose: Cross-system curriculum placement for the Grade 1-6 geometry concepts in the MathBridge taxonomy.

verification_policy.CN: Use the 2022 MOE mathematics standard at learning-stage level. Detailed content is marked partially verified where the official document identity is verified but machine-readable page extraction is supplemented by curriculum transcriptions and public education-platform material. Exact current PEP grade/semester remains separate.
verification_policy.UK: Use the statutory National Curriculum in England year-by-year programmes of study.
verification_policy.US: Use Common Core State Standards as the comparison baseline. Record concepts that are not explicit Grade 1-6 Common Core expectations rather than forcing alignment.

stages.expectation: Recognise common plane figures such as rectangles, squares, parallelograms, triangles and circles and describe visible features.
Study lines, angles, triangles and quadrilaterals more formally and classify figures by properties.

placement.expectation: Recognise and name common 2-D shapes.
Describe, compare and sort 2-D shapes by properties.
Draw 2-D shapes and extend property language.
Compare and classify geometric shapes including triangles and quadrilaterals.
Draw, compare and classify shapes using increasingly specific properties.
Reason about defining attributes and compose 2-D shapes.
Recognise and draw shapes with specified attributes.
Reason about shared attributes and categories of quadrilaterals.
Classify 2-D figures using line and angle properties.
Classify 2-D figures hierarchically by properties.

stages.expectation: Recognise common solids such as cuboids, cubes, cylinders and spheres and describe visible features.
Study cuboids, cubes, cylinders and cones, their features and relationships, and connect solids with nets and measurements.

placement.expectation: Recognise and name common 3-D shapes.
Describe properties using faces, edges and vertices and identify 2-D shapes on surfaces.
Make 3-D shapes and recognise them in different orientations.
Identify cubes and other cuboids from 2-D representations.
Recognise, describe and build simple 3-D shapes including nets.
Compose common three-dimensional shapes into composite shapes.
Recognise shapes with specified attributes, including cubes.
Represent 3-D figures with nets and use them for surface-area problems.

stages.expectation: Classify simple plane and solid figures using observable features.
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by geometric properties.

placement.expectation: Compare and sort common 2-D and 3-D shapes and everyday objects.
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals based on properties and sizes.
Distinguish regular and irregular polygons and use rectangle properties.
Compare and classify shapes and find unknown angles from their properties.
Distinguish defining from non-defining attributes.
Recognise hierarchical relationships among quadrilaterals.
Classify figures by parallel/perpendicular lines and angle size.
Classify 2-D figures in a hierarchy.

CN.expectation: Understand relationships between two lines in a plane, including parallel and intersecting/perpendicular lines; identify and construct examples using appropriate tools.

placement.expectation: Identify horizontal/vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines.
Use conventional markings and properties involving parallel lines in shape reasoning.
Draw and identify parallel and perpendicular lines and classify figures by their presence or absence.

stages.expectation: Recognise simple plane figures including rectangles, squares and parallelograms.
Recognise and classify triangles and quadrilaterals, including parallelograms and trapezoids, from their properties.
Use triangle and polygon properties in measurement and reasoning, including triangle side and angle relationships.

placement.expectation: Handle and name quadrilaterals and polygons and describe their properties.
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals.
Distinguish regular and irregular polygons.
Find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons.
Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons and hexagons.
Understand quadrilateral subcategories.
Classify 2-D figures using line and angle properties.
Use hierarchical classification of 2-D figures.

stages.expectation: Recognise a circle as a common plane figure.
Recognise circles and sectors, draw circles with a compass, understand pi, and investigate circumference and area.

placement.expectation: Recognise and name circles as common 2-D shapes.
Name and use radius, diameter and circumference and know that diameter is twice the radius.
Partition circles into equal shares as part of early fraction work.
Partition circles into equal shares.

US.notes: Common Core does not introduce radius, diameter or circumference as a Grade 1-6 geometry requirement; detailed circle measurement appears later.

CN.expectation: Recognise angles in life contexts and connect angle to geometric configuration; graph-motion work also develops intuitive turning/rotation ideas.

placement.expectation: Describe whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.
Describe rotation as turn and connect quarter/half/three-quarter turns to right angles.
Recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn.
Understand angle measurement by reference to turning through a fraction of a circle and define degree measure.

CN.expectation: Compare angle sizes and understand that angle size is measured independently of side length; use degree measurement in later work within the stage.

placement.expectation: Identify whether angles are greater than or less than a right angle.
Compare and order acute and obtuse angles up to two right angles.
Estimate and compare acute, obtuse and reflex angles and measure them in degrees.
Understand degree measure and measure/draw angles in whole-number degrees.

CN.expectation: Identify right, acute and obtuse angles and recognise straight and full angles; use angle properties to classify triangles.

placement.expectation: Identify right angles and compare angles with a right angle.
Identify acute and obtuse angles.
Identify acute, obtuse and reflex angles.
Draw and identify right, acute and obtuse angles and classify shapes using angle size.

CN.expectation: Use a protractor to measure angles and use a ruler/protractor or set square to construct specified angles.

placement.expectation: Know angles are measured in degrees, draw given angles and measure them using a protractor.
Measure angles in whole-number degrees with a protractor and sketch angles of a specified measure.

stages.expectation: Relate angle categories and use angle properties when classifying triangles.
Know that the interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees and use geometric relationships in reasoning.

placement.expectation: Use angle facts at a point, on a straight line and multiples of 90 degrees; deduce missing angles.
Find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons and use vertically opposite angle facts.
Use additivity of angle measure to find unknown angles in diagrams.

US.notes: Common Core does not require the full England-style set of point/straight-line/triangle angle relationships in Grades 1-6.

stages.expectation: Relative-position and direction ideas occur in integrated/practical contexts rather than as a large formal geometry sequence.
Determine position using direction and distance from a reference point and describe simple routes.

placement.expectation: Describe position, direction and movement including whole/half/quarter/three-quarter turns.
Use precise position, direction and movement language.
Describe positions on a grid and movements as translations.
Represent and interpret position with coordinates in the first quadrant.

US.notes: Common Core has relative-position language in Kindergarten, outside MathBridge Grade 1-6 scope; the next explicit coordinate-position work is Grade 5.

CN.expectation: Use ordered pairs of natural numbers to represent point locations and understand the correspondence between ordered pairs and points on squared paper.

placement.expectation: Describe positions on a 2-D grid as coordinates in the first quadrant and plot specified points.
Continue using first-quadrant coordinates with reflection and translation.
Describe positions on the full coordinate grid in all four quadrants.
Define a coordinate system and graph/interpret points in the first quadrant.
Use all four quadrants and draw polygons from coordinates.

stages.expectation: Recognise/experience axial symmetry in real examples.
Recognise axis-symmetric figures and axes of symmetry and complete simple symmetric figures on squared paper.

placement.expectation: Describe line symmetry in a vertical line as a property of 2-D shapes.
Identify lines of symmetry and complete a symmetric figure.
Use reflection on grids as a transformation.
Reflect shapes in coordinate axes.
Recognise and draw lines of symmetry for 2-D figures.

stages.expectation: Experience translation in examples and describe its visible effect.
Translate simple figures on squared paper and use translation in design/pattern contexts.

placement.expectation: Describe movements between positions as translations left/right and up/down.
Identify, describe and represent translated shapes and know the shape is unchanged.
Draw and translate simple shapes on the coordinate plane.

US.notes: Formal translation as a geometric transformation is introduced later in Common Core, not as a Grade 1-6 geometry standard.

stages.expectation: Experience rotation in examples and identify rotation phenomena.
Rotate simple figures on squared paper, including simple quarter-turn cases, and use rotation in pattern/design contexts.

placement.expectation: Use whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.
Use rotation language for turns, clockwise and anticlockwise.

UK.notes: Later primary England programmes focus more explicitly on translation and reflection; formal coordinate-plane rotation is not a Year 5-6 statutory strand.

placement.expectation: Use turning through a circle to define angle measure, but this is not a standard for rotating figures as a transformation.

US.notes: Formal rotation of figures as a transformation appears later than Grade 6.

cross_system_notes: China 2022 separates geometry into shape/measurement and position/movement themes, with more formal point-location and figure-movement work in Grades 5-6.
England gives a detailed year-by-year statutory progression and includes translation/reflection within upper-primary position and direction.
Common Core has strong Grade 4 line/angle/symmetry content and Grade 5-6 coordinate content but does not require translation or rotation of figures as Grade 1-6 transformations.
